findings.reason: §2/§3 must state `domain.py`'s disposition (absorbed into `topology.read`, or retained-with-reason like the `moment.py` exception) or the §6 deletion gate has a collision the node will discover only at retirement.
findings.text: `domain.py` is the plasma-region classification authority (`classify_domains`, `axis_connected_component` at :172, `saddle_qualified_domains` at :222) and is imported by ten modules including `topology.py` (being replaced in place) and `forward_operator.py`; the plan's text never mentions it (0 occurrences of `domain` in the plan HTML), yet §2 requires the read to decide membership "sub-cell and axis-connected" and §3 requires private-flux exclusion "because membership is axis-connected before any sub-cell polygon is clipped" — the precise computation `axis_connected_component` owns today. The §6 census clause as written ("no module under `nova/equilibrium` other than `topology.py` locates a null or classifies a region") would fail outright on `domain.py` at retirement, and §2 could re-implement axis-connectivity behind `topology.read` rather than absorb or explicitly retain the owner.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design hides substantial behaviour (the sub-cell axis-connected membership read, the exact-clip booking, the composed map with its implicit Picard, moment-map and boundary-envelope derivatives, and Newton-GMRES with one line search) behind four functions `read`/`book`/`apply`/`fixed_point`, one call site each; this is depth, not a fan of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan names no disposition for `nova/equilibrium/domain.py`, the module that owns plasma-region classification (`classify_domains`, `axis_connected_component`, `saddle_qualified_domains`, `PlasmaDomain`, `DomainMasks`), while §3's booking and §2's membership clause are both defined in terms of exactly that axis-connected region.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — the supplied counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the sections that could grow a family name their retirements in their own text (§6's request-surface ruling collapses `SolveRoute`'s six members to one solve, deletes `SupportClipMode` with the chord modes, and removes eight plumbing fields from `ForwardSolvePolicy`; §2 and §5 state their policy operands are carried by `ForwardSolvePolicy` "extended rather than duplicated"). No section adds surface to a counted family without accounting for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched both codebases it names and cites the mechanism each new module extends: the GMRES kernel, the line-search scoring, the Newton machinery, `polygon_moments.py`, `contour_tree.py`, the clip helpers, the operand layouts and the moment-map derivative are each named candidates carried into the new module or declined with a stated contract failure; the cited files (`fixed_point.py`, `reduced_newton.py`, `clip_quadrature.py`, `polygon_moments.py`, `contour_tree.py`, `forward_operator.py`, `topology.py`) all exist at the stated sizes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every added layer states what it replaces rather than what it wraps: `gs.apply` "replaces the map `ForwardFluxOperator` performs today rather than wrapping it", `forward.py` shrinks to the request/receipt adapter, and each cite-or-justify ruling directs the node to extend the owning mechanism or justify declining it, never to sit a parallel layer beside it.
